display_name: Resolution in the high southern latitudes, 1773-1774 (sample)
notes: Four points standing for a two-year track. It is a sample that proves the schema carries a line, not a route anyone may measure. The real track is compiled at ANT-5 from the journals.

A planned route is an intention, not an observation, and this drawing of it is ours. It is filed as editorial_interpolation so that no part of the pipeline can mistake it for evidence, which is the distinction Act VIII turns on.

display_name: Endurance in the ice, besetment to loss (two-point sample)
notes: Two endpoints joined by a straight line, which the drift certainly was not. Present only to prove the schema can hold a drift distinct from a planned route; ANT-9 replaces it with dated positions.

display_name: James Caird, Elephant Island to South Georgia (noon positions from the log)
source_locator: Appendix B (pp. 58-66), noon positions for Days 1 to 15
notes: Fifteen vertices: the departure position and the noon position the log carries for each day of the passage, in the log's own figures. It replaces the three-point sample whose middle point was ours entirely - the line is now Worsley's track and not our drawing of one, which is what derived_from_log rather than editorial_interpolation records. Where a day has both a reckoned and an observed position the observed one is the vertex, because that is the position the log carried into the next day's run; both survive as rows in observations.csv, and a test asserts the vertices are exactly those positions. Two cautions the line cannot carry itself. The class is dead_reckoning because most of these noons are reckoned - five of the fourteen are corrected by sights - and filing the whole track as a fix would overclaim the nine that are not. And a noon-to-noon line says nothing about the path between two noons; the passage ends at the 8 May position because that is the last one the log works, with the landing two days later carried by ant-obs-king-haakon-bay.

display_name: Endurance from South Georgia into the Weddell Sea (sample)
notes: The last stretch under the ship's own power, held apart from the drift that follows it so that the moment the vessel stops navigating is a change in the data and not only in the prose.
